- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–15% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, apply a 10–20% downward correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (especially in first 10 days), assume mean reversion and adjust downward by 3–8% for next period.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is high, apply a 5–10% downward bias to reflect pessimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show strong downward trend in true outcome, reduce forecast’s early peaks by 10–15%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.3–0.5) over 3–5 days, apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecast.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >10% across 3+ consecutive days, assume model overestimates and reduce by 5–10% for next forecast.
